copy.headline: More counties look to Tarrant agency for water as North Texas growth drives demand
copy.caption: Parker, Wise, Johnson, Ellis counties are forming utilities, undertaking studies to identify how North Texas surface water can meet demands. The Tarrant Regional Water District’s service area could expand as the surface water needs of communities west of the county grows, compounding North Texas’ increasing water demands.

story.title: More counties look to Tarrant agency for water as North Texas growth drives demand
story.summary: Parker, Wise, Johnson, Ellis counties are forming utilities, undertaking studies to identify how North Texas surface water can meet demands. The Tarrant Regional Water District’s service area could expand as the surface water needs of communities west of the county grows, compounding North Texas’ increasing water demands. The water district is engaging in conversations with officials from regional planning groups consisting of counties and municipalities across Wise and Parker counties, chief engineering officer Rachel Ickert shared with board directors Tuesday. That involves the West Fork and Parker County public utility agencies. While yet to be officially established, 13 municipalities have expressed interest in joining the Parker County regional utility, said Parker County commissioner Larry Walden, who is heading the agency’s formation.
